title: Memory Leaks
concept: Memory leak: A phenomenon in which the remaining memory is depleted due to borrowing and not paying back.

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
Header for using `printf`.

This example is a counterexample that intentionally causes a memory leak.

steps.title: Include stdlib.h header
steps.explanation:
Header for using `malloc`.

If `free` is omitted, leaks will accumulate.

steps.title: leak function definition
steps.explanation:
The `leak` function allocates heap memory but does not free it.

Even if the pointer disappears after the function ends, the heap block remains and causes a leak.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created and ready to repeatedly call `leak`.

steps.title: Start loop (i=0)
steps.explanation:
Repeated calls create a situation where leaks accumulate.

The number of unrecoverable heap blocks increases by the number of iterations.

steps.title: leak() function call #1
steps.explanation:
On the first call, a new heap block is allocated.

It is still possible to access it through pointers inside the function.

steps.title: exit leak() function #1
steps.explanation:
The function ends without release, and the first leak is confirmed.

This is because the pointer pointing to that heap block has disappeared.

steps.title: Water leak message output #1
steps.explanation: Outputs the status of the first water leak.

steps.title: Continue loop (i=1)
steps.explanation:
Enter the second iteration.

Existing leaks remain unresolved.

steps.title: leak() function call #2
steps.explanation: Allocate an additional second heap block.

steps.title: exit leak() function #2
steps.explanation:
It also terminates without release, confirming the second leak.

The total amount of leakage is accumulated.

steps.title: Water leak message output #2
steps.explanation: Outputs the second leak accumulation status.
steps.stdout:
Memory leaked 1 times
Memory leaked 2 times

steps.title: Loop continues (i=2) ...
steps.explanation:
The same pattern repeats itself, with leaks continuing to increase.

This accumulation is fatal for long-running processes.
steps.stdout:
Memory leaked 1 times
Memory leaked 2 times
Memory leaked 3 times

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Even though the OS reclaims memory when the program terminates, leaks during execution create major performance and stability problems.

The principle is simple: if you `malloc` something, you must `free` it.

quiz.question: How to prevent memory leaks?
options: free must be called for every malloc
I hope the operating system takes care of it.
quiz.explanation:
Java and Python have a garbage collector (GC), but C and C++ do not.
The programmer must take 100% responsibility.

misconceptions.wrong: When the program ends, the leaked memory does not return.
misconceptions.correct: Once terminated, the operating system reclaims everything.
misconceptions.why: However, water leaks can be fatal in programs that are turned on 24 hours a day, such as servers, or in games that run for a long time.

keyTakeaway: Lost addresses cannot be found again. If you did `malloc`, take full responsibility.
